items.question: What does Avesta Tech do?
items.answer: We help software and connected-product makers prove their code is secure and tested. Our product, Avesta Proof, turns scans into signed, audit-ready evidence for ISO/IEC 27001, IEC 62443-4-1 and the EU Cyber Resilience Act. We also deliver fixed-price quality, test automation and accessibility services.

items.question: Does Avesta Proof replace an audit or a certification?
items.answer: No tool can do that, and we will not pretend otherwise. Avesta Proof produces audit-ready evidence: a verdict per control, signed reports and a technical-file draft. Certification and conformity decisions come from accredited bodies and your own assessment.

items.question: Does my source code leave my company?
items.answer: No. Avesta Proof runs in your CI or on your own machine, including air-gapped machines. Only the signed results move, and only if you send them.

items.question: Which languages and stacks do you support?
items.answer: Semgrep covers many languages. Python gets extra checks from Bandit, C and C++ from cppcheck. Dependency scanning works through Trivy. SBOMs are generated from Python, npm and Cargo lock files today, with Maven, Gradle, Go, yarn, pnpm and NuGet on the roadmap.

items.question: How is this different from Snyk or SonarQube?
items.answer: Those tools are good at listing issues for developers. Avesta Proof answers a different question: "Can we prove it to an auditor?" It maps findings to controls in three standards, signs the result, tracks expiring manual evidence and drafts the CRA technical file.

items.question: Who is behind Avesta Tech?
items.answer: Avesta Tech was founded in Utrecht in 2026 by Mohammad Ali Shikhi, a software and test automation engineer with high-tech industry experience. You work directly with engineers, not account managers.

items.question: How can my auditor check a report?
items.answer: With one command and our public key: `avesta-proof verify report.json --pubkey avesta-proof.pub`. It checks the fingerprint and the Ed25519 signature offline. `verify-ledger` checks that no earlier scan was removed or changed.

items.question: What happens when a tool is not installed?
items.answer: The controls that tool supports are marked partial, never pass. A scanner that does not apply, such as cppcheck on a Python-only project, is marked not-applicable and does not count against you.

items.question: Why do you charge per product and not per developer?
items.answer: Regulation applies to products. Charging per product keeps your price tied to what you need to prove, so growing your team does not raise your bill.

items.question: Is there a free option?
items.answer: Yes. The Community edition gives developers the command-line tool and local reports. The CRA readiness checker on this site is free too.

items.question: Are prices including BTW?
items.answer: No. All prices exclude 21% Dutch BTW. For business clients outside the Netherlands, VAT is handled according to EU rules; your invoice will show it clearly.

items.question: Can I start with a service and move to a subscription later?
items.answer: Yes, and most teams do. A CRA Readiness Scan gives you a first signed report and a plan. If you want the evidence kept current every week, a Team plan picks up from there.

items.question: Can I cancel?
items.answer: Monthly plans can be cancelled with [NOTICE_PERIOD] notice. Your reports and ledger stay yours; they are files you own.

items.question: When does the Cyber Resilience Act apply?
items.answer: The Regulation entered into force on 10 December 2024. Reporting duties for actively exploited vulnerabilities have applied since 11 September 2026. Most other obligations apply from 11 December 2027.*
items.footnote: * Dates and amounts: verify with counsel.

items.question: What are the penalties?
items.answer: For the main obligations, fines can reach EUR 15 million or 2.5% of worldwide annual turnover.* Your counsel can tell you how this applies to you.
items.footnote: * Dates and amounts: verify with counsel.

items.question: Does the CRA apply to my product?
items.answer: It covers most products with digital elements sold in the EU, with some sector exceptions. The checker gives a first indication; confirm with counsel.

items.question: What is a technical file?
items.answer: The technical documentation a manufacturer keeps to show how the product meets the essential requirements (Annex VII of the Regulation). Avesta Proof drafts it from real scan data; your team completes and reviews it.
